neighbours.label: A speaker talking in their own voice near the start of a text: first-person pronouns (I, we, me, also in other languages) and one-word spoken interjections (Yeah, Wait, Oh, Okay, Hmm) in the opening clause; plain noun subjects and impersonal prose stay low, and third-person pronouns fire only weakly.
fire: I think the bus is going to be late again.
Yeah, that sounds like a plan to me.
Wait, did you leave the oven on?
We finally finished painting the kitchen last night.
Oh, I forgot my umbrella at the office.
Okay, let me try that one more time.
Hmm, I'm not sure that key fits this lock.
Je pense que nous devrions partir tôt demain.
quiet: Wesley Weber wrote the memo on Wednesday.
Did the volunteers grab the extra chairs?
The bus is going to be late again, according to the schedule.
That plan was approved by the committee.
The oven was left on overnight in the empty bakery.
The kitchen was finally painted last night.
The umbrella remained at the office all week.
The procedure must be repeated one more time.

predictions: Blind test written from the label only. Risk: sentence-initial 'I'/'We' read lower than mid-clause pronouns in probes (~0.29); interjection openers should carry it.
short: speaker's own voice: I/we/me and Yeah/Wait/Oh openers
